Answer: B
Reason: The ultrasound images show a hyperechoic mass with cystic spaces in the fetal thorax (indicated by arrows), consistent with a congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) or bronchopulmonary sequestration. Such lesions, particularly when located in the middle or lower lobes, often cause mass effect leading to mediastinal shift (displacing the heart to the contralateral side) and elevation of the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm due to volume expansion within the confined thoracic cavity. Option B accurately describes this classic presentation of a space-occupying cystic lung lesion causing displacement of adjacent structures.
